target_customer: Fintech, crypto, marketplaces, iGaming and mobility companies and governments needing identity verification and fraud checks, including firms new to ID verification
problem: Identity verification vendors are expensive and bundled with contracts and minimums; developers want one API for KYC, KYB, AML, biometrics and fraud with pay as you go pricing.
business_model: Usage based API with a free tier and per check pricing

founders.name: Alberto Rosas
founders.background_notes: Former professional tennis player per YC page; identical twin of Alejandro. No prior employers or education listed by sources opened.

founders.name: Alejandro Rosas
founders.background_notes: Former professional tennis player per YC page. No prior employers or education listed by sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: Document and biometric verification, liveness and aggregation of 1,000+ data sources are standard but compliance heavy; in house models claimed by the company.

defensibility.rationale: Many incumbents and fast followers. Company claims validation in Spain's Financial Sandbox, unverified, which may help in Europe.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept offering similar products; no acquisition of Didit found as of 2026-11.

market_need_then: KYC and fraud demand rose with regulation and AI generated fraud. Company says 80% of its customers had not used an ID provider before. Pricing from $0.30 per call and a free tier is the wedge, per the company's own pages.

branding.domain_note: Uses didit.me, not an exact .com; business portal at business.didit.me.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and developer friendly: integrate in minutes, pay as you go, start free

branding.brand_signature: Identical twin founders who were professional tennis players, per the YC page
branding.community_and_virality: Press on the twin founder story in a Japanese outlet, The Bridge; no merch or community evidence found

brand_strength.rationale: A short playful name with a non standard domain, and a memorable founder story, but little brand coverage beyond funding news.

outcome_analysis: Didit is an active Winter 2026 company that announced a $6M seed on 2026-05-26, bringing total seed financing to $7.5M, according to its own blog and press. It claims 1,500 customers, growth over 30% month over month and profitability, all self reported. Success so far rests on aggressive pricing and a free tier in a crowded market, so durability depends on whether those economics hold.
notes: Company blog says $6M round and $7.5M total; Biometric Update (opened) confirms, dated May 27 2026. Dealroom and Forgenex describe the same round as EUR 6.4M; CB Insights lists $6M total, probably outdated. An earlier tranche of about $1.5M is only implied by subtraction and not recorded. Round date 2026-05-26 from the company blog. Founder roles CEO and CTO from the YC page. Competitor list drawn from Didit's own comparison pages so partly self serving; competitor traction at 2023 not found.
